name: discord
description: Discord support parity: same graph as Slack, different event source. Tests that the evaluation harness correctly routes discord-sourced questions through the support surface.

cases.name: discord-mention-question
cases.input: What is the difference between authly.permissions.check() and authly.roles.assign()? When should I use each?
cases.expected_output: permissions.check() validates whether a user has a specific permission — it is a read-only assertion that raises AuthorizationError if denied. roles.assign() grants a role to a user, which changes their permission set. Use check() to gate access in your application logic; use assign() to manage role membership (e.g. during onboarding or admin actions).

evidence.excerpt: authly.permissions.check(user_id=user.id, permission='documents:write') raises AuthorizationError if not allowed.
authly.roles.assign(user_id=user.id, role_id=role.id) assigns the role to a user so that permission checks pass; assignments are stored as a set of user IDs on the role.
